newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends flat to down slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends flat to down slightly.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were mostly unchanged near the close Tuesday, though traders said prices deteriorated slightly in spots.
The muni market's trend this week has been to remain in a narrow range, mindful of Friday's inflation data in the Producer Price Index for September.
The market Tuesday again closely tracked Treasuries, where the long bond was off 6/32 at 99-10/32. The yield moved to 6.80 percent on the price erosion.

In the muni secondary, bids on Denver Airport MBIA 5-1/2s of 2025 were one basis point lower at 5.77 percent net. Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, Ill., AMBAC 5-1/4s of 2027 were down two basis points to 5.78 percent.

Afternoon repricings included Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency's $75 million mortgage revenue bond issue. PaineWebber adjusted yields in several maturities but left the top tax-exempt yield in 2027 unchanged at 6.15 percent.
PaineWebber said it had $15.8 million of bonds remaining on Virginia Housing Development Authority's $58.6 million mortgage revenue bond deal, which the firm won in competitive bidding Tuesday.

The debt futures markets closed down slightly. The December municipal contract was 4/32 lower at 115-15/32 and December T-bonds fell 2/32 to 111-3/32. That widened the MOB spread between the two contracts to 140 ticks, compared to 138 ticks at the close Monday.
Wednesday's new deals feature $301 million of negotiated offerings, including a $120.6 million North Carolina Medical Care Facilities Authority through senior manager Smith Barney Inc.

The competitive calendar for Wednesday totals $193 million in five offerings. The largest is a AAA-rated $170 million Maryland general obligation bond deal at 1100 EDT, which analysts said they will be watching closely as a market gauge.

"Maryland is a super bellwether," one analyst said. He said the state's bonds usually fare slightly better than AAA averages in an up market and slightly worse in a down market, making it an unusually accurate measure of levels.
